input.rationale: Use public RawNode bootstrap, campaign, proposal, application and transfer APIs; no internal writes or fabricated peer responses. One FIFO transport serializes actual emitted messages and transiently drops MsgTimeoutNow through ten ticks. All persistence/apply/Advance work is processed synchronously, with transfer legally interposed between ApplyConfChange and Advance for the joint entry. A no-transfer control has identical configuration input. Selected private fields are read-only diagnostics to distinguish queue depletion from incomplete setup; no state-cycle claim is made. No crashes occur, so MemoryStorage completion substitutes for durable media. The driver stops after forty ticks plus independently scheduled diagnostic proposal, not upon failure to exit.
input.question: For candidate 8b412541680b42dd938dc9d5945e1aed, can actual three-node producers reach application-completion rejection during a transfer, then remain joint after transfer timeout while transport, required ticks and Ready handling continue? Does an independently scheduled later proposal restore exit? Finite checkpoints are construction observations, not a deadline oracle or proof of infinite stalling.

result.summary: Submitted a preflight-validated exploration using three real RawNodes, transient transfer-message loss, continued ticks and Ready processing, a no-transfer control, and a later diagnostic proposal. Execution is pending; no defect or indefinite stall is asserted.

materials.text:
First, you must read from the Node.Ready() channel and process the updates
it contains. These steps may be performed in parallel, except as noted in step
2.

1. Write HardState, Entries, and Snapshot to persistent storage if they are
not empty. Note that when writing an Entry with Index i, any
previously-persisted entries with Index >= i must be discarded.

2. Send all Messages to the nodes named in the To field. It is important that
no messages be sent until the latest HardState has been persisted to disk,
and all Entries written by any previous Ready batch (Messages may be sent while
entries from the same batch are being persisted). To reduce the I/O latency, an
optimization can be applied to make leader write to disk in parallel with its
followers (as explained at section 10.2.1 in Raft thesis). If any Message has type
MsgSnap, call Node.ReportSnapshot() after it has been sent (these messages may be
large).

Note: Marshalling messages is not thread-safe; it is important that you
make sure that no new entries are persisted while marshalling.
The easiest way to achieve this is to serialize the messages directly inside
your main raft loop.

3. Apply Snapshot (if any) and CommittedEntries to the state machine.
If any committed Entry has Type EntryConfChange, call Node.ApplyConfChange()
to apply it to the node. The configuration change may be cancelled at this point
by setting the NodeID field to zero before calling ApplyConfChange
(but ApplyConfChange must be called one way or the other, and the decision to cancel
must be based solely on the state machine and not external information such as
the observed health of the node).

4. Call Node.Advance() to signal readiness for the next batch of updates.
This may be done at any time after step 1, although all updates must be processed
in the order they were returned by Ready.

Second, all persisted log entries must be made available via an
implementation of the Storage interface. The provided MemoryStorage
type can be used for this (if you repopulate its state upon a
restart), or you can supply your own disk-backed implementation.

Third, when you receive a message from another node, pass it to Node.Step:

	func recvRaftRPC(ctx context.Context, m raftpb.Message) {
		n.Step(ctx, m)
	}

Finally, you need to call Node.Tick() at regular intervals (probably
via a time.Ticker). Raft has two important timeouts: heartbeat and the
election timeout. However, internally to the raft package time is
represented by an abstract "tick".

the library is different from what was presented above. Users still read from
the Node.Ready() channel. However, they process the updates it contains in a
different manner. Users no longer consult the HardState, Entries, and Snapshot
fields (steps 1 and 3 above). They also no longer call Node.Advance() to
indicate that they have processed all entries in the Ready (step 4 above).
Instead, all local storage operations are also communicated through messages
present in the Ready.Message slice.

The local storage messages come in two flavors. The first flavor is log append
messages, which target a LocalAppendThread and carry Entries, HardState, and a
Snapshot. The second flavor is entry application messages, which target a
LocalApplyThread and carry CommittedEntries. Messages to the same target must be
reliably processed in order. Messages to different targets can be processed in
any order.

Each local storage message carries a slice of response messages that must
delivered after the corresponding storage write has been completed. These
responses may target the same node or may target other nodes.

selections.rationale: Retain initial sourced core relationships and retry surfaces while the backbone remains incomplete. No Candidate, obligation or execution result is asserted.

feedback.answered: A1 learning: leader proposals append term/index-tagged entries; self acknowledgments and follower append/vote responses wait for persistence. Leader response handling updates Progress, attempts current-term commitment and broadcasts advancement. JointConfig requires both constituent majorities. A2 learning: higher-term messages ordinarily trigger follower transition with explicit pre-vote and lease exceptions; old-term replies are ignored, while old storage snapshot completions retain meaning as committed state. reset clears votes, replication progress and read-only tracking but retains the log. becomeLeader appends an empty entry and conservatively defers configuration proposals behind the inherited tail. Applied configuration changes the voter tracker used by formation and election. Application completion differs from durability: MsgStorageApplyResp is term-independent; ordinary RawNode.Advance dispatches precomputed completions, and heartbeat-only Ready batches do not create application acknowledgments. Early surface: AutoLeave promises implementation-owned transition when possible. appliedTo attempts an empty configuration proposal, but stepLeader rejects proposals during leadership transfer. The retry comment refers to the next advance after failed transfer, whereas tickHeartbeat timeout calls abortLeaderTransfer, whose body only clears leadTransferee. This discrepancy is an unresolved retry premise, not a demonstrated violation.
remaining: Complete initial core overview through campaign aggregation, follower append matching, snapshot restore, persistence reconstruction and configuration changer validation. This partial learning does not establish map readiness.

Investigate whether a legal Ready/application schedule can place the only automatic exit attempt during transfer, followed by transfer timeout without further unapplied entries. Read caller duties, existing tests and alternative retry triggers before execution.

Independent surface: switchToConfig can advance commitment and broadcast without the pending-read release call present in MsgAppResp handling. Determine whether pending reads can legally exist then and whether another consumer necessarily releases them.
feedback.rationale: Preserve producer/consumer distinctions. Durability ordering and term filtering counter an immediate stale-ack safety allegation. Automatic exit can succeed on ordinary application completion or a new leader applying its empty entry; these protections do not yet answer the failed-transfer/no-new-application premise.

selections.rationale: Record usable initial two-core map and select sourced automatic configuration-transition retry question, retaining independent limits and counterevidence.

feedback.answered: Completed the representative backbone and mapped acquired learning. The suspected missing pending-read release in switchToConfig is not by itself a completion defect: Node.ReadIndex explicitly permits loss and requires caller retry. Automatic joint exit has a separate implementation-owned when-possible contract. Existing auto-leave test covers leadership loss/reacquisition, while RawNode Advance only generates an application response for nonempty committed entries, preserving the failed-transfer quiet-suffix question.
remaining: Can a legal history commit joint entry and start transfer before Advance without forcing another application completion later?
Do any caller obligations require new proposals or another trigger after a failed transfer, beyond ticks and Ready processing?
Can all in-flight appends, callbacks and queues be accounted for in a quiet suffix, rather than mistaking finite waiting for lost continuation?
feedback.rationale: Separate documented caller retry from automatic configuration duty; preserve the unsuccessful-transfer discriminator rather than expanding guard-only tests.

formation.explanation: A1: a leader assigns term/index to proposals, appends unstable entries and replicates through peer Progress. Local and remote append support is published after persistence. Responses pass term dispatch and known-peer checks, update Match and contribute only through current configured voter majorities; joint commitment is the minimum of the two majority-supported indexes. maybeCommit advances only when that index has current term. Advancement broadcasts to followers; matching append constrains follower commit to received prefix, heartbeat producer caps it by peer Match, and committed conflicts cannot overwrite history. Ready exposes committed entries with applying cursor and size controls; caller applies configurations and state-machine entries, then completion updates applied. Rejected appends backtrack; heartbeat responses reopen flow and snapshots catch up compacted peers.

context.explanation: A2: eligible voters campaign only without unapplied committed configuration or pending snapshot. Real campaign increments term, records self vote durably and requests votes using last log term/index; configured majority votes acquire leadership. Pre-vote preserves local term until its quorum succeeds. Leader acquisition resets volatile support and appends a current-term empty entry. Higher terms normally step down with lease/pre-vote exceptions; old replies are discarded. Quorum loss can step down; transfer selects a caught-up voter, drops proposals while active and expires after electionTimeout if still leader. Restart restores HardState/configuration and enters follower. Existing committed decisions remain valid across authority changes; old storage snapshots and term-independent application completion remain consumable, while entry-stability acknowledgment requires matching generation.

connection.explanation: Applied membership determines support eligibility for both election and log commitment. Joint config requires both old and new majorities; recovery restores that same configuration, not a fresh quorum. Term reset clears votes and peer progress but retains committed history; log freshness and committed-prefix guards constrain subsequent formation. The new leader conservatively sets pendingConfIndex to inherited last index. Config proposals cannot overtake unapplied changes under normal validation. Automatic joint exit depends on application completion and leader role, and uses ordinary proposal admission, so an active transfer can reject it. Ordinary Ready completion only issues an apply acknowledgment for nonempty committed entries. readOnly support resets with authority, while pending pre-current-term reads have a distinct release path; their cross-context details remain open and their external API assigns retries to callers.

Fine-grained asynchronous snapshot/application overlap and resource-error recovery.

implementation_guards: Joint entry requires no existing outgoing configuration; simple change modifies at most one voter; resulting incoming voters nonempty; voters and learners cannot overlap.
writes: Incoming/outgoing voters, learners and staged learners, AutoLeave, Progress; pending transfer may be aborted on transferee removal.
important_branches: Entering joint preserves old voters; leaving joint clears outgoing and AutoLeave and finalizes learners.
switchToConfig may advance commitment under changed quorum, broadcasting append without calling releasePendingReadIndexMessages.
Removed/demoted leader optionally steps down; absent self blocks new proposals.

cross_activity_effects.A2: Config determines election votes, promotability and transfer eligibility.

unknowns: Can configuration-driven first current-term commitment leave pending reads without an implementation trigger? ReadIndex explicitly requires caller retries, so absence alone is not a completion violation.

after.protocol_context: Local term, leader role and voter set
after.trigger: Tick/campaign, vote replies, higher-term message, quorum check
implementation_guards: Campaign requires voter eligibility and no pending snapshot or unapplied committed configuration.
Vote requires voting eligibility in term and up-to-date candidate log; response aggregation uses configured voters and both joint majorities.
writes: Term, Vote, leader, state, election timers; reset votes, peer progress and readOnly on reset.
important_branches: Pre-vote does not increment term; real candidacy increments term and votes for self after durability.
Higher-term vote may be ignored during valid lease; higher-term pre-vote grant does not cause stepdown.
Old-term messages generally discarded; old append-storage response may still apply committed snapshot.
Leader acquisition appends current-term empty entry; prior committed log retained and inherited tail constrains new configuration proposals.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Resets support tracking across authority transitions; term matching prevents counting old-term append support as a new leader response.

unknowns: pendingReadIndexMessages survives reset while readOnly is replaced; exact cross-term pending-request consequences remain unexamined.

after.protocol_context: Follower log under term-qualified leader message
implementation_guards: Append predecessor term/index must match; conflicting committed entry panics; append truncation cannot cross committed prefix.
writes: Unstable suffix, leader, election elapsed, committed index
external_effects: Append acknowledgment waits for storage; rejection carries index/term hints; heartbeat acknowledges context.
important_branches: Append commits at most received matching suffix end.
Heartbeat producer caps advertised commit at min(peer Match, leader commit).
Append below local commit acknowledges already committed position.

after.protocol_context: Leader term and active voter configuration
implementation_guards: Reject empty proposals, absent self membership, transfer-in-progress, or size excess.
Append responses require known Progress and pass term dispatch; quorum index must match current term to advance commitment.
writes: Appended term/index entries, per-peer Match and inflight state, monotone committed index
external_effects: Broadcast append on new commitment; release queued pre-current-term reads only in the successful MsgAppResp commit branch.
important_branches: Configuration proposals become empty normal entries when pending/unapplied or invalid joint phase, unless validation explicitly disabled.
Self append acknowledgment is deferred until storage completion.

after.protocol_context: Ordered persistence batches and term-qualified storage completion
after.trigger: Ready acquisition and subsequent persistence completion
legal_preconditions: Serialized RawNode access; persist and apply Ready work in documented order; do not mutate entries; AsyncStorageWrites local target queues are reliable and ordered.
durable_effects: Durability itself belongs to embedding caller; MemoryStorage is in-memory storage implementation.
external_effects: Return entries/HardState/snapshot and messages; route durability-dependent responses after storage.
important_branches: Synchronous Advance steps self responses and storage acknowledgments.
Asynchronous writes encode append/apply work as local messages; no Advance allowed.
Stale storage completion does not discard unstable entries; current-term storage completion after HardState term update can stabilize them.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Prevents publishing support before local persistence.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Persists term and vote and correlates unstable completion with current authority generation.

after.protocol_context: Restart or follower snapshot catch-up
implementation_guards: Reject obsolete snapshot; recipient must be present in configuration; restore only follower.
Matching snapshot term/index fast-forwards commitment rather than replacing log.
HardState commit must lie in retained log bounds.
writes: Restore committed prefix and unstable snapshot or reconstruct term, vote, applied cursor and configuration.
important_branches: Fresh construction reads Storage.InitialState and restores config with validation then enters follower.
Snapshot recovery rebuilds tracker and voter configuration; snapshot remains pending until storage/application acknowledgment.
Compacted replication uses recently active peer snapshot; unavailable snapshot returns for later retry.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Snapshot represents already committed prefix, not newly aggregated support.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Recovered configuration controls eligible participation; pending snapshot blocks campaigning.

after.meaning: The node has accounted for successful application through an index.
after.validity_context: Committed prefix; completion remains meaningful after term changes and is distinct from Ready issuance.
after.durability: Caller owns durable state-machine progress and supplies Config.Applied/recovered snapshot.
after.recovery: newRaft initializes from compacted prefix and optional Config.Applied.

after.meaning: The local raft instance has a role, term and known leader used to dispatch and qualify protocol messages.
after.validity_context: Role/leader may change within a term; real elections increment term; lease/pre-vote rules qualify handling of future-term requests.
after.durability: Term and vote in HardState; role and leader volatile.
after.recovery: newRaft restores term/vote then becomes follower.

after.meaning: The node records a prefix as committed, eligible for ordered application subject to local storage and flow-control requirements.
after.validity_context: Commitment is monotone across local term changes; leader advancement requires current-term quorum support, followers learn bounded commitment from matching append/heartbeat or snapshot.
after.durability: HardState.Commit and snapshot/log state are persisted by caller.
after.recovery: loadState validates stored commit within log; snapshot establishes committed index.

after.meaning: This instance has an active voter/learner configuration, optionally joint with AutoLeave selected.

identity.configuration: incoming/outgoing voters and learner sets installed by ordered ApplyConfChange or recovered ConfState

after.validity_context: Until subsequent accepted configuration application or snapshot restoration; joint configuration with AutoLeave true selects automatic exit but does not assert that an exit proposal is queued.
after.durability: ConfState is caller-recorded in snapshots; configuration entries are persisted in the log.
after.recovery: confchange.Restore reconstructs incoming/outgoing groups and AutoLeave from stored ConfState.

formation.explanation: A1: a leader assigns term/index to proposals, appends unstable entries and replicates through peer Progress. Local and remote append support is published after persistence. Responses pass term dispatch and known-peer checks, update Match and contribute only through current configured voter majorities; joint commitment is the minimum of the two majority-supported indexes. maybeCommit advances only when that index has current term. Advancement broadcasts to followers; matching append constrains follower commit to received prefix, heartbeat producer caps it by peer Match, and committed conflicts cannot overwrite history. Ready exposes committed entries with applying cursor and size controls; caller applies configurations and state-machine entries, then completion updates applied. Rejected appends backtrack; heartbeat responses reopen flow and snapshots catch up compacted peers.

context.explanation: A2: eligible voters campaign only without unapplied committed configuration or pending snapshot. Real campaign increments term, records self vote durably and requests votes using last log term/index; configured majority votes acquire leadership. Pre-vote preserves local term until its quorum succeeds. Leader acquisition resets volatile support and appends a current-term empty entry. Higher terms normally step down with lease/pre-vote exceptions; old replies are discarded. Quorum loss can step down; transfer selects a caught-up voter, drops proposals while active and expires after electionTimeout if still leader. Restart restores HardState/configuration and enters follower. Existing committed decisions remain valid across authority changes; old storage snapshots and term-independent application completion remain consumable, while entry-stability acknowledgment requires matching generation.

connection.explanation: Applied membership determines support eligibility for both election and log commitment. Joint config requires both old and new majorities; recovery restores that same configuration, not a fresh quorum. Term reset clears votes and peer progress but retains committed history; log freshness and committed-prefix guards constrain subsequent formation. The new leader conservatively sets pendingConfIndex to inherited last index. Config proposals cannot overtake unapplied changes under normal validation. Automatic joint exit depends on application completion and leader role, and uses ordinary proposal admission, so an active transfer can reject it. Ordinary Ready completion only issues an apply acknowledgment for nonempty committed entries. readOnly support resets with authority, while pending pre-current-term reads have a distinct release path; their cross-context details remain open and their external API assigns retries to callers.

open_details: Automatic exit after failed transfer with no new application completion.
Configuration-driven pending-read release and pendingReadIndexMessages across terms; caller retries constrain obligations.
Fine-grained asynchronous snapshot/application overlap and resource-error recovery.
after.rationale: Representative formation, authority, membership, persistence, rejection/retry, recovery and consumption paths are traced. Local questions remain; this map does not imply comprehensive safety or API coverage.

Does changed-quorum commitment leave pending requests behind, and what responsibility remains given the explicit caller retry contract?

after.system_boundary: Captured go.etcd.io/raft/v3 library including RawNode/Node, log, tracker, configuration and MemoryStorage. Embedding transport, durable medium and state machine are external interfaces; their in-library coordination remains in scope.
protocol_contexts: Node identity, election term, per-node role, ordered log index, applied voter configuration
Crash-fault assumptions with caller-compliant persistence and message production; no Byzantine fabricated messages
ownership: RawNode is thread-unsafe and serialized by caller; Node owns a channel-select loop.
Application owns storage persistence, state-machine execution, configuration application and transport.

selections.rationale: Use public RawNode bootstrap, campaign, proposal, application and transfer APIs; no internal writes or fabricated peer responses. One FIFO transport serializes actual emitted messages and transiently drops MsgTimeoutNow through ten ticks. All persistence/apply/Advance work is processed synchronously, with transfer legally interposed between ApplyConfChange and Advance for the joint entry. A no-transfer control has identical configuration input. Selected private fields are read-only diagnostics to distinguish queue depletion from incomplete setup; no state-cycle claim is made. No crashes occur, so MemoryStorage completion substitutes for durable media. The driver stops after forty ticks plus independently scheduled diagnostic proposal, not upon failure to exit.
